content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tutorial: High Availability with MySQL Router and AdminAPI"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial covers deploying and configuring MySQL InnoDB Cluster using MySQL AdminAPI and routing client traffic efficiently with MySQL Router. By the end of this guide, you will have a fault-tolerant database architecture."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Three MySQL Server instances running version 8.0 or higher."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"MySQL Shell installed on your management node."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"MySQL Router installed on your application gateway or load balancer node."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Creating the InnoDB Cluster via AdminAPI"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, open MySQL Shell and connect to your first instance to bootstrap the cluster using JavaScript mode."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"mysqlsh --js -uroot -p -h mysql-node1.local --port 3306"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create the cluster object and add the instances."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"var cluster = dba.createCluster(\"myCluster\");\ncluster.addInstance(\"root@mysql-node2.local:3306\");\ncluster.addInstance(\"root@mysql-node3.local:3306\");"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Checking Cluster Status"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Verify that all instances are online and properly replicating by running the status command."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"cluster.status();"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Configuring MySQL Router"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"MySQL Router sits between your applications and the InnoDB Cluster, routing read-write queries to the primary instance and read-only queries to secondaries. Bootstrap the router using the mysqlrouter command."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"mysqlrouter --bootstrap root@mysql-node1.local:3306 --directory /var/run/mysqlrouter --user mysqlrouter"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Starting MySQL Router"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Start the newly configured MySQL Router service to begin accepting client connections."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"systemctl start mysqlrouter"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"You have successfully established a highly available MySQL InnoDB Cluster managed through AdminAPI and scaled client connectivity safely using MySQL Router."}]
